reason: Eventar MVP execution works through card files in docs/plans/mvp with a LOCK file and a fixed hand-back template. The episode followed the template by hand (CX-01, DB-01). Writing it down keeps later cards consistent and makes deviations and unverified claims visible to Ivan.

Ivan repeatedly said "keep going one task after another", then "pause at the next checkpoint". The card-handback skill says nothing about continuing or pausing between cards. The design-pick handoff also gave only ids and a preview link, not the options, against Ivan's at-least-3-options rule.

The agent found that the card's blanket instruction would have broken presenter and chair assignment. It applied the database rule and surfaced the question. That is the behaviour the handback skill should make standard.

The old line said "remove it whatever the outcome", which conflicts with a paused card that must keep its lock. It also gave no atomic-create method. CX-05 was paused as PARTIAL with its LOCK kept, and the doc says so.

CX-07 was blocked because its fix needed components/auth/auth-error-messages.ts, which the card did not list and CX-06b reserved. The hand-back skill had no rule for this stop, so the blocked-card format was improvised.

During UX-03 a motion dependency appeared in package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml that none of the cards added. Q41 forbids new dependencies without Ivan's ask, and the hand-back skill had no check for this.

The phase completion protocol requires three separate review lenses (dev, user, backtest) on each card before the card is presented. The hand-back must record each lens's outcome, and the user asked for the review protocol after each task.

Review fixes applied as MECHANICAL were reported as "applied and tests green" with no before→after diff. The frontend rule says the review that follows must show the difference for every mechanical change, so the hand-back must list each one.

The Committer role in this episode filled the Committed: lines in a follow-up docs commit and verified them with grep -c -x; the skill says nothing about how the field is filled or where the commit procedure lives. Pointer added to the new commit-procedure skill.

Executor stopped PARTIAL because the card's May-edit list named a route folder (app/dashboard/manage/**) but the page copy lives in components/dashboard/ManageWorkstation.tsx. The coordinator then had to add the file. Also the PARTIAL-to-finished handoff had no rule for how the hand-back records the coordinator's additions. Both are gaps in this skill.
The executor cited two line numbers that were wrong on first write (497 and 570, real 499 and 569) and fixed them only after writing the doc. A grep before the doc is final would have caught both.
DB-03 dev-lens review found header and card-doc claims ("UI is tightened", "(tested)") with no app file changed and only one of several tables tested. The hand-back must match what shipped.

Episode marked a card STATUS: DONE while admitting the three-lens review was not run ("the brief did not ask for it"). The skill's rule says a card is not presented until all three lenses report, and the project protocol requires them for every phase. The status line must match that rule so a skipped review cannot read as done.
